brief: A desktop PDF toolkit for Windows whose standout feature is Document Assembly: drop in PDFs and images, pick pages from any of them, and export one new document. Everything stays on your computer. It should feel fast, clear and trustworthy, like a well-made tool.
criteria: Success: distinct from red PDF badges and plain dog-eared pages, clear on a 24 px Windows taskbar, works in one colour, and fits the app's dark interface and amber accent.
label: Final design

concepts.name: The Weld
concepts.idea: Two sheets interlock around a new page, the hot spot where they fuse: Document Assembly as forge-welding.
rationale: Draws the product's standout feature instead of a generic document
Two identical sheets, rotated 180 degrees, give it a steady, engineered balance
Amber is already the app's accent colour, and here it means heat
Three drawings keep it sharp at 16 px, at 24 px and at full size

next_steps: Replace the placeholder app icon in build/ with the new one
Add the logo to the README and the app's sidebar
